claims.text: Three-dimensional NM-HEA nanoframeworks can be produced by combining in situ aberration-corrected STEM with molecular dynamics simulations.
Noble metal-based high-entropy alloys have diverse compositions.
Noble metal-based high-entropy alloys have complex surface structures.
In situ aberration-corrected STEM can be combined with molecular dynamics simulations to investigate NM-HEA nanoparticles.
The relevant thermal conditions extend up to 973 K.
An AuCu layer forms at the nanoparticle surface at high temperature.
The surface AuCu layer melts at high temperature.
Progressive phase separation in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles is driven by pronounced atomic diffusion.
Atomic diffusion is more active in the quinary AuCoCuNiPt nanoalloy than in monometallic and bimetallic subsystems.
The observed phase separation and diffusion produce three-dimensional NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
The resulting three-dimensional NM-HEA nanoframeworks have enhanced thermal stability.
The resulting three-dimensional NM-HEA nanoframeworks have enhanced structural properties.
Traditional superalloys have limited high-temperature strength and stability.
The application-temperature boundary for the proposed material is 973 K.

contradictions.description: The mechanism field confidently states that pronounced atomic diffusion drives phase separation, while the uncertainty field says that the exact phase-separation mechanism and the role of atomic diffusion remain uncertain.
Enhanced thermal stability and structural properties are asserted as outcomes, but the experiment supplies no comparator, metric, or threshold defining what counts as enhanced.
